notice: CUSTOM 13-MODULE ASSESSMENT PROFILE. The titles and descriptions below use the 13 modules supplied by the project team. This is not the official OWASP Top 10 list: modules 11-13 are supplementary assessment areas. Entries are enabled as manual-review items only; they do not perform automated detection. Implement and validate a check before treating any module as automatically verified.

rules.title: Broken Access Control
rules.description: Checks whether users can access only the resources and actions permitted by their roles and ownership. Review authorization on every protected endpoint, object-level access, privilege boundaries, and default-deny behavior.
rules.recommendation: Enforce authorization on the server for every request. Apply least privilege, verify resource ownership, deny by default, and test horizontal and vertical privilege boundaries.

rules.title: Security Misconfiguration
rules.description: Reviews application, server, framework, cloud, and deployment settings for unsafe defaults, unnecessary services, exposed debug features, verbose errors, and unintended public access.
rules.recommendation: Use secure configuration baselines, disable debug mode in production, remove unused components, restrict administrative interfaces, and review deployment settings regularly.

rules.title: Software Supply Chain Security
rules.description: Reviews third-party packages, build tools, container images, and update processes for known vulnerabilities, untrusted sources, abandoned dependencies, and integrity risks.
rules.recommendation: Maintain an inventory of dependencies, pin and verify versions, scan for known vulnerabilities, remove unused packages, and obtain components from trusted sources.

rules.title: Cryptographic Failures
rules.description: Reviews how sensitive data is stored, transmitted, and protected, including password storage, encryption choices, key handling, and accidental exposure of secrets.
rules.recommendation: Use established, modern cryptographic libraries and protocols, hash passwords with a purpose-built password hashing algorithm, protect keys and secrets, and avoid storing unnecessary sensitive data.

rules.title: Injection
rules.description: Reviews whether untrusted input can be interpreted as SQL, operating-system commands, templates, or other executable expressions.
rules.recommendation: Use parameterized database queries and safe APIs, avoid constructing commands from user input, validate input by context, and encode output appropriately.

rules.title: Insecure Design
rules.description: Reviews application architecture and business workflows for missing security controls, unsafe trust assumptions, abuse cases, and design-level weaknesses.
rules.recommendation: Perform threat modeling, define security requirements, identify abuse cases, apply secure design patterns, and include security review in design changes.

rules.title: Authentication Failures
rules.description: Reviews identity verification and session handling, including password policy, account recovery, brute-force protections, session expiration, and multi-factor authentication where appropriate.
rules.recommendation: Use a trusted authentication framework, protect account recovery, rate-limit authentication attempts, use secure session handling, and support multi-factor authentication for sensitive accounts.

rules.title: Software and Data Integrity
rules.description: Reviews whether software updates, build artifacts, serialized data, and other trusted inputs can be modified or consumed without integrity verification.
rules.recommendation: Verify update and artifact integrity, protect build and deployment pipelines, validate data before trusting it, and avoid deserializing untrusted data unsafely.

rules.title: Security Logging and Alerting
rules.description: Reviews whether security-relevant events are recorded, protected, monitored, and escalated without exposing passwords, tokens, or other sensitive information.
rules.recommendation: Log authentication and authorization events, validation failures, and important administrative actions; protect logs from tampering; redact secrets; and configure useful alerts.

rules.title: Exception Handling
rules.description: Reviews how the application handles unexpected conditions, failed dependencies, invalid states, and runtime errors, including whether errors disclose internal details.
rules.recommendation: Handle expected errors explicitly, return safe and consistent error responses, keep detailed diagnostics in protected server logs, and avoid exposing stack traces or secrets to clients.

rules.title: API Security
rules.description: Reviews API-specific protections such as endpoint authorization, object-level access, rate limits, resource consumption, method restrictions, and exposure of unnecessary data.
rules.recommendation: Apply authentication and authorization to every relevant endpoint, enforce object-level permissions, limit request rates and payload sizes, validate methods and content types, and return only required fields.

rules.title: Input Validation
rules.description: Reviews whether data from clients and other untrusted sources is validated for type, format, length, range, and allowed values before processing.
rules.recommendation: Validate inputs at the application boundary with explicit schemas and allowlists where practical. Enforce size and range limits, reject malformed data, and do not rely on client-side validation alone.

rules.title: Security Headers and Browser Protection
rules.description: Reviews browser-facing response protections, including content security policy, transport security, clickjacking defenses, MIME sniffing protections, and cookie security attributes.
rules.recommendation: Configure appropriate security headers for the deployment, use HTTPS, set secure cookie attributes, and test the policy against the application's actual browser features and resource requirements.
